name: Motion Poster
visualIdentity: A complete, readable poster first: clear headline, imagery, supporting information, and negative space. Motion selectively animates elements or rearranges the layout while preserving useful still frames. A normalized style label based on a moving street-poster description.
suitableUses: Explicitly suits announcements; suggested fits include event and film posters, social posters, hero banners, UI and product storytelling, editorial layouts, and staged geometric compositions. The pinned-hero pattern is suitable when continuous recomposition helps explain the subject. These are suitability cues, not guarantees.
limitations: Recomposition should clarify the subject and preserve hierarchy. Avoid crops that hide important details or push text into unsafe areas. For interactive pages, pinning must fit the page and release without a jump. Video must not depend on live scrolling. Keep headlines readable during transitions and match loop endpoints. Omit the pinned-hero pattern if it adds no explanatory value.
palette: No intrinsic palette is specified. Preserve task, brand, reference, semantic-role, and asset colors. If none exist, an optional three-token example is background #F4EDDF, foreground #273B44, accent #B66A4B; use discrete colors, with the accent for decoration rather than normal text on it. Gradients are disabled. Preserve color roles and families; do not recolor subjects or expand approved palettes. Check contrast on actual composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Build the still layout, then use local loops, layout changes, or controlled boundary crossings with readable text holds and matched loop endpoints. Optional pinned-hero recomposition keeps the stage fixed while internal elements separate, a focal form expands, the central headline clears, and supporting copy moves outward without a cut. For web, map finite scroll progress to inner wrappers, then release without a jump. For video, drive states from seekable composition time, independent of live input. Preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, and reading holds; verify backward and direct seeks.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or audio layer is specified. Choose music, voice, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject and audience, honor supplied choices, and avoid competing with essential text or speech. Synchronize and inspect picture and sound together.
assetRequirements: Use authorized artwork and exact copy; retain headline clearance, safe crops, subject context, and motion margins. Load fonts and assets before animation. Optional Cropper.js can prepare crops; preserve the source and crop recipe and inspect exported quality. It does not extract subjects, remove backgrounds, or create missing artwork. Optional tldraw can author diagram assets, but flattened exports need deliberate layer separation for independent animation.
combinations: Screen-printing style-051 can reinforce event or film posters with three inks—navy, rust, cream paper—sequential ink reveals, and no gradients. Style-101 can add restrained image-area parallax while text stays static; disable pointer tilt under reduced motion. Keep still frames useful and avoid parallax on headlines. These combinations are suggestions, not requirements.
productionApproach: Use HTML/CSS for layout and SVG for scalable shapes, masks, and strokes; choose only needed tools. GSAP is the registered seekable timeline; optional Motion, mo.js, or Anime.js require verified time synchronization and distinct property ownership. HyperFrames is the primary composition/export pipeline; Remotion is allowed only if unavailable or a verified required capability is blocked, with reason recorded. Pipelines do not replace visual or motion design. For interactive image galleries, PhotoSwipe is optional and does not generate artwork or play poster animation.
